newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asiana plans Seoul-Frankfurt 747 Combi in May 97.
newsitem.headline: Asiana plans Seoul-Frankfurt 747 Combi in May 97.

text.p: South Korea's Asiana Airlines plans to begin flying between Seoul and Frankfurt twice weekly from next May using Boeing 747 Combi aircraft, cargo director Tae Sin Kang told Reuters in a telephone interview.

He also said Asiana has been given permission to increase its Combi services to Belgium and Austria. The current schedule is a once weekly flight between Seoul, Brussels, Vienna and Seoul and once weekly Seoul, Vienna, Brussels, Seoul. From mid-May next year, Kang said Asiana will fly twice weekly between Seoul and Brussels and twice weekly between Seoul and Vienna.
With the proposed Frankfurt link, Asiana will have six Combi flights a week from Seoul to Europe, Kang added.
Korean Air and Lufthansa Cargo AG operate a freighter service between Seoul to Frankfurt six times a week in a code share arrangement.
Industry sources said the use of combis is being seen as a way round current restrictions on Asiana starting full freighter flights to Europe.

Asiana's ambitions to begin its first scheduled freighter service to Amsterdam are currently stalled because South Korea's flag carrier Korean Air is the designated carrier in a code share agreement with KLM, the sources said.

Asiana, now seen as South Korea's second carrier and growing rival to Korean Air, has said it is aiming to get into the world top ten of cargo carriers within three years and the start of a European service will be a turning point for its entire air cargo business.

However the sources added that Korea's Ministry of Transportation and Construction guidelines currently restrict Asiana to charter flights only to Amsterdam and bilateral talks held between the Dutch and South Korean governments in February failed to satisfy Asiana.

Kang said he is now hoping for a breakthrough at new aviation talks to be held between the Dutch and South Korean governments in the Hague on December 10 and 11. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44-171-542-7706 Fax+44-171-542-5017
